answer: Argon2 registration puzzles make every identity pay in RAM. First, a new agent solves an Argon2id puzzle needing 2 GB of memory and about 40 minutes of compute. Second, the solution is signed into a registry entry that expires after 30 days. Third, renewal repeats the puzzle with fresh salt, so stockpiling fails. Fourth, peers attest only agents holding a live entry. Forging 10,000 identities needs 20 TB of RAM for a month, about $60,000 in cloud rent. Picture a vine climbing toward a summit: every leaf grows its own stem, and nectar reaches only leaves that did.
